announcements.text: vpn/services/gatus/config/config.yaml carries live credentials in plaintext, including SSH private-key blocks. Never grep it with a context flag (-A/-B), and never print a parsed form of it - json.dumps of a single endpoint dict renders the key field verbatim. Read the KEY NAMES only; to compare a value, hash it in place. The read discipline is necessary but not sufficient: the PRINT is the second chokepoint, and it is the one that fails when the read felt safe. A third chokepoint is any TOOL whose output path renders the file's content: a diff, a checksum-and-dump, or a guard that prints a drift diff between two key-bearing copies discloses both. Read the output path before you ship the tool, not after.

announcements.text: A Gatus alert page can be SILENTLY LOST: the relay on vpn forwards it over an SSH hop to the agents host's A2A gateway, and when that hop fails the receiver records delivered=false (transport_error) and the target lane is never woken. THIS ENTRY PREVIOUSLY SAID "the owner's q16 ACCEPTS the loss" — that citation is WITHDRAWN as a misattribution, not because the defect healed. q16 is a different question (the notify forward leg's ack-wait budget: "its ack-wait budget has been outgrown twice and its delivered verdict can no longer increment — which shape?"), answered 2026-10-02T12:33:31Z with "Trust the notify queue - the notifications always land. If they are list, it's not a problem" — an assertion that notifications LAND, which is the opposite of an acceptance that one can be lost. So no owner acceptance of page loss exists, and no factory may cite one. The warning stands on its own measurement: do not treat a Gatus page as a guaranteed wake — verify the episode in the receiver's store or the ledger when the alert matters, because a failed forward leaves no trace in the topic it should have woken.

If they are list, it's not a problem" — quoted in full so the next reader can judge the citation rather than inherit it. Re-verified 2026-11-21T09:10Z, and the defect is LIVE, not historical: the gatus-notify relay on vpn is active, and over journald's FULL retained window (from 2026-11-16T09:22:09+03:00; the journal holds nothing for Nov 14-15) the invocation `journalctl -u gatus-notify --since 2026-11-14` carries 9 'Alert delivery FAILED after 3 attempt(s)' lines - seq=444, 446, 448, 450, 453, 454 (Nov 16), 458, 459 (Nov 17), 466 (Nov 18) - every one rc=4 transport_error 'cannot reach the A2A gateway at http://127.0.0.1:18791/a2a/v1'. Against 83 'Alert delivered to session' lines that is 9/92 = 9.78% loss (90.22% delivered), failures 6/2/1 by day, and Nov 19-21 carries ZERO. CORRECTION 2026-11-21, measured by the Triage lane and reproduced on this host: this entry previously read 'carries 5 ... seq=453, 454, 458, 459, 466' and 'Latest observed loss 2026-11-20T19:42Z'. Both were wrong. The cited invocation returns 9, not 5, and the enumeration dropped four Nov-16 losses (444, 446, 448, 450); and the 2026-11-20T19:42 event was a RECOVERED DELIVERY, not a loss - attempts 1/3 and 2/3 failed rc=255 'ssh: connect to host 78.17.187.4 port 15259: Connection timed out' and attempt 3/3 DELIVERED at 19:42:48, 30 s after the first try. The rc=255 shape is real as a SHAPE but has not caused a loss on this relay. Latest observed loss is 2026-11-18T09:10:54Z (seq=466). The CLASS stands on the 9 measured losses at ~10%, not the ~70% asserted in conversation. Absent alert is still not evidence the endpoint was healthy. RETENTION CORRECTION 2026-11-21T22:20Z: the SAME invocation (`journalctl -u gatus-notify --since 2026-11-14`) now returns 5 'Alert delivery FAILED after 3 attempt(s)' lines, not 9, because journald's retained window for this unit now begins 2026-11-16T20:07:08+03:00 (MaxRetentionSec=7day, SystemMaxUse=512M, 214.1M in use): the four Nov-16 morning rows seq=444, 446, 448, 450 have ROTATED OUT, and the survivors are seq=453 (2026-11-16T20:07:33+03), 454 (21:19:40+03), 458 (2026-11-17T16:19:11+03), 459 (16:54:15+03) and 466 (2026-11-18T12:10:54+03).
